issues.description: README diff silently changes StorageError.handle signature, breaking the documented contract
issues.detail: The README now declares handle(req, resp, ex, params), but Falcon's add_error_handler historically expects (ex, req, resp, params) for the legacy form. If a reader copies this README example verbatim, the error handler will be invoked with swapped arguments. Either the README is wrong, or this is an undocumented API change that needs a literate comment explaining the new order.

issues.description: FAQ example reads req.content_length bytes but the test sends Content-Length: 1 with an empty body, masking a subtle invariant
issues.detail: req.stream.read(1) on an empty body returns b'' in the test harness, so the example happens to return 400. But the stated invariant ('non-zero Content-Length with empty body returns 400') is not what the code proves; the code proves 'read() returned falsy'. State the invariant explicitly, or the next reader will mis-extend this pattern. The literate explanation is missing.

issues.description: Switch from req.stream.read() to req.bounded_stream.read() is unexplained in the example
issues.detail: The substantive behavioral change in things_advanced.py is replacing stream with bounded_stream, but no comment justifies why. Bounded vs unbounded stream semantics matter for correctness under chunked encoding and oversized bodies. A reader studying the example cannot derive the rationale from the code alone; a one-line literate comment is owed here.

issues.description: New tests assert only status codes; the invariant being tested is not stated
issues.detail: resp3 asserts 201 and resp4 asserts 400, but neither test has a docstring or comment naming the property under test ('POST with valid JSON body succeeds'; 'POST with empty body but non-zero Content-Length is rejected as malformed'). Tests are documentation of invariants. Without the naming, a future maintainer cannot tell whether 400 is the intended contract or an accident of bounded_stream behavior.

issues.description: FAQ code sample has style issues that contradict 'write for the reader'
issues.detail: The example uses `assert(result.status == ...)` (parenthesized as if a function call), a trailing comma in `[('Content-Length', '1'),]`, and an unused `import falcon` (only HTTP_200/201/400 referenced via the class). Small things, but FAQ code is read carefully by newcomers learning idiomatic Falcon. Tighten before merging.

issues.description: No negative test for the inverse case (zero Content-Length, non-empty body) or for the malformed-JSON branch
issues.detail: The PR adds two POST tests but leaves the JSONTranslator's malformed-JSON path (lines 116-124 of the example) and the missing-'thing' path uncovered. If the stated goal is auditing POST behavior of things_advanced, the coverage is incomplete. Not a blocker, but the proof-by-testing is partial; worth a follow-up case.

review.summary: UNDER-AUDITED and NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT. The behavioral substance of this PR is small (two new POST tests, one stream-to-bounded_stream swap, one FAQ entry), but the rigor around it is thin: the new tests state status codes without naming invariants, the bounded_stream swap is uncommented, and the FAQ example proves a weaker property than its prose claims. The README diff also flips StorageError.handle's parameter order, which deserves either a versionchanged directive or a correction. None of this is wrong-by-analysis; it is under-audited and under-explained. A reader cannot pick this up and learn the invariants from the code alone, which for example/FAQ code is the whole job.
